chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Yahya ibn al-Mubarak, from Abdullah ibn Jabala, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a neighbor of mine and what I endured from him. He said to me: 'Supplicate against him.' I said: 'So I did, but I did not see anything.' So I returned to him and complained to him. He said to me: 'Supplicate against him.' I said: 'May I be sacrificed for you, I have done so, but I did not see anything.' He said: 'How did you supplicate against him?' I said: 'When I met him, I supplicated against him.' He said: 'Supplicate against him when he turns his back and when he faces you.' So I did it, and I did not delay long before Allah gave me rest from him.

key_terms.أَرَاحَ اللَّهُ مِنْهُ: Allah gave me rest from him

ai.seo_question: How did the Imam instruct to supplicate effectively against a difficult neighbor?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the practical application of *du'a* as a spiritual weapon against oppression, highlighting the Imam’s guidance on precision in supplication rather than mere repetition. The specific instruction to invoke divine retribution when the neighbor turns his back (*idbira*) and faces him (*istidbar*) reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on timing and presence of mind in spiritual combat. It underscores the belief that persistent, targeted supplication, even when results seem delayed, ultimately leads to divine relief (*faraj*).
